addendum.multi_call_diagnosis_basis: predicted call count is the length of the call array recovered from each sealed response text by reproduction.toolcall_scoring.parse_tool_calls_text, the same parse both registered scorers run; every row's parse outcome was asserted equal to the parsed flag the scorer sealed for that row, so the counts are a faithful reconstruction of what the scorer itself saw. An unparsed row counts as 0 calls, exactly as the scorer treats it. For the native-tools arms the transport canonicalizes each message.tool_call 1:1 into that array, so for a natively-arriving row this count IS the number of tool_call entries the envelope carried; per-row native counts are not themselves sealed (only per-cell totals are, in the run_phases receipt), so the canonicalized array is the faithful proxy. Gold call counts come from data.audio2tool.load_expected_calls, the scorer-side gold path, reduced to a length before anything is recorded.
addendum.ordered_vs_multiset_basis: read verbatim from each cell's sealed SAEA-A2T-DIRECT-CALIBRATION-V1.scores.json (a2t-toolcall-v2 aggregate and its per_tier block). For every cell and tier the v2 tool_accuracy_multiset column was asserted equal to the v1 a2t-toolcall tool_accuracy column, which is what identifies v2's tool_accuracy as the ordered variant rather than a relabelled multiset.
addendum.tier1_wrong_tool_set_basis: a tier1_direct row counts as wrong when its sealed a2t-toolcall (v1) tool_accuracy is below 1.0, i.e. the predicted tool-NAME multiset differs from gold's. Rows that emitted exactly one call against exactly one gold call are split by where the predicted tool_name sits relative to gold's in the tools_registry.csv domain/category taxonomy (3 domains, 28 (domain, category) families over 152 tools). FOUR buckets are reported rather than the two the question names, because the question's own exemplar -- setLighting vs setLightState -- is same-domain but CROSS-category (smart_home/core_control vs smart_home/lighting): scoring 'same family' as 'same domain AND category' alone would classify that exemplar as a different family and would report zero near-neighbour substitutions for both legacy cells. near_neighbour_same_domain recombines the two same-domain buckets and is the figure that answers the question as intended; the cross-domain buckets stay split because a substitution landing on the same category LABEL in another domain (status -> status, security -> security, maintenance -> maintenance) is a device-domain confusion rather than a naming one. Rows that failed to parse, or that emitted a different number of calls than gold, are reported separately because no single-name substitution is defined for them.
